source_text.gate: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate for REQ-519 slice 2f-b (GH #2535), uncommitted tree on feature/WF02-REQ519-2FB-ON-SETTABLE-20261019. A foreign mixlock (ELIXIR-DEV-2661) was present at the start; I waited for it to disappear (never removed it), then took the lock with mkdir and released it after the last mix command. One mix at a time, per file, no full suite, no letflow.check.test, no real tenant set to on.

task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER 2f-b tests: REQ-519 ACs 8, 12 (docs), 13, 14 (wiring), 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24; SEC step-21 merge conditions; REVIEWER step-22 notes; judge the UNCOVERED items and the 8 surviving mutants; own mutants; isolation, formatting, flake and CI-environment risks.

result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. EXECUTED (MIX_ENV=test, mix compile --force first: 504 files, exit 0, no warning): every 2f-b file green per file, default log level and the four log-heavy files again at LOG_LEVEL=error: transitions 36, routers/tenant_scope_enforcement_on 24 (22 + my 2), flip_authority 14, route_scope_on_flip_blocker 8, roles_on_flip_docs 14, on_e2e 8, on_flip_guards 17, binding_no_row_report 16, scope_enforcement_on_test 16 (the T-O1 migration-down tests: no stale on tenant left); no compiler warning in any run; mix format --check-formatted exit 0 on all ten files created or edited. 17 own in-memory mutants (details below): every non-equivalent one killed; the 8 survivors of the designer are ruled: MU-37a, MU-37b, MU-37d, MU-53, MU-T-O8/b/c EQUIVALENT or covered elsewhere; MU-37c was a REAL gap (a platform-tenant user holding PLATFORM_ADMIN plus only a scoped TENANT_ADMIN row passes checks 1, 2, 3 and was stopped by check 4 alone, untested): I added a test, now killed. The designer's UNCOVERED list is acceptable (see findings F-2..F-4). The blank-vs-missing reason difference: the AC text should move, not the code (F-1).

A comment records which single-check mutants are equivalent and why. First test names exceeded the 255-character atom limit (SystemLimitError at compile time) and were shortened before any measurement was recorded.

The platform tenant is the one place where the tenant-wide permission check passes on the PLATFORM_ADMIN shortcut, so a platform user with a scoped-only TENANT_ADMIN grant passes every other check. Without this test a regression removing check 4 would have let a scoped admin flip enforcement in the platform tenant unnoticed.

findings.title: AC 13 wording: 'missing or blank: reason_required' does not match the code; the AC should move
findings.detail: The code answers reason_required (422) only for a MISSING reason (nil: check_reason(:off, nil) before the transaction; on -> shadow inside the transaction) and invalid_reason (422) for a blank, whitespace-only, multi-line or over-long one (Audit.Reason.validate), exactly as stage 1 did for shadow -> off. That stage-1 behaviour is pinned by unedited stage-1 tests (test/letflow/routers/tenant_scope_enforcement_test.exs line 397-408: no reason -> reason_required; invalid -> invalid_reason) and AC 13 itself says off -> shadow 'keeps the stage-1' behaviour. Changing the code would change the stage-1 contract and break those tests; both are 422, nothing is written, no information leaks. The tests (T-X9, router) pin the implementation correctly.
findings.required_action: DOC-UPDATER: amend AC 13 to 'missing: reason_required; blank or invalid: invalid_reason; both 422, nothing written' and list it in the PR body behaviour notes. No code change.

findings.title: AC 16 data-path bullets are not re-driven after a REAL flip
findings.detail: Query/aggregate/export/cursor totals, by-id indistinguishability, moving a record out of scope, import with one out-of-scope row, undeclared types and the scoped approver are proven by the REQ-518 suites under stored on (entities_scope_*, tasks_scope_http_test, attachment_link_scope_test, scope_gate_test) which set the column through the fixture. The flip only writes the column and the data path reads it per request, so the marginal value of re-driving them after the PUT is low; T-Z1 proves the real flip changes the tenant-wide route class, the admin plane, the writers, the sync and the way back byte-identically. AC 16 says 'one suite'; that literal form is not met.
findings.required_action: Acceptable to leave. The PR body should state that AC 16's data-path clauses are covered by the REQ-518 suites (names above) and the e2e file covers the flip itself; if the supervisor insists on the literal single suite, extend OnGateFixture.backdate_shadow! + real flip with the entities_scope_http harness as a follow-up.

findings.title: RefusedAudit called inside the flip transaction is a no-op by design; the mutant that only adds such a call is equivalent
findings.detail: RefusedAudit.record/6 refuses inside an open transaction (writes nothing, logs scope_enforcement_refusal_not_recorded). My first form of the 'refusal audit inside the transaction' mutant (add an in-transaction call, keep the post-rollback call) therefore survived (77 passed): equivalent. The real form (move the call inside: in-transaction call plus the post-rollback call disabled) is killed 7+ ways (T-A6, every AC 14 refusal test, T-H5/T-H7).

findings.title: Flake and CI-environment review
findings.detail: Held-lock tests share the existing 700 ms per-phase deadline (a loaded host can only produce a false failure, never a false pass). Day-count tests: the HTTP flip tests backdate the shadow entry 8 days and cover request counters from -9 to +1 days (a run across UTC midnight is covered); flip-level tests use fx.now = t0 + 7 days of the real flip entry (moves with t0); the one real-clock assertion in on_flip_guards uses a 300 s tolerance. No Process.sleep in any new file. Scan and docs tests are async: true with no database, read the working tree via cwd-relative globs, and the temp-dir test uses a unique directory removed in on_exit. Runtime of the 2f-b files on this host: 33 + 29 + 5 + 1 + 0.1 + 8 + 17 s (about 95 s plus about 70 s boot overhead). Stale _build: mix compile --force before measuring. LOG_LEVEL both ways: default (debug) and error, 24 + 17 + 36 + 8 passed under error. Hard facts on log capture (with_log captures Ecto debug QUERY lines) are respected: every assertion extracts the constant marker line.

findings.title: purge_stale_enforced_tenants!/1 safety
findings.detail: Lives in test/support (compiled only for MIX_ENV=test: elixirc_paths(:test) = [lib, test/support]); called from exactly one place (the setup of the T-N5 describe of binding_no_row_report_test). It deletes only tenants whose slug starts with the caller's prefix (LIKE metacharacters escaped), stored on, updated more than ten minutes ago; per-tenant try/rescue with a logged skip (total). It cannot touch a real tenant: no real slug starts with req519-n5-mix, and tests run against the test database only. Concurrent run risk: a tenant of a parallel run of the same file is minutes old at most (the file takes 25 s), well inside the ten-minute guard. Verified by running: binding_no_row_report 16 passed and scope_enforcement_on_test 16 passed after it (no stale on tenant left).

findings.title: AC 24 lib-side scan limits
findings.detail: The scan catches literal on pairs in lib/ (AST), SQL and bulk setters in lib/ and priv/, any changeset caller other than scope_enforcement.ex, any flip caller other than the router, and text in priv/config/scripts/.github/mix.exs. A variable-valued setter in lib/ (Ecto.Changeset.change(t, scope_enforcement: var)) is not caught by the pair scan; it would be caught only if it went through scope_enforcement_changeset. Acceptable (SEC-level residual, the column is set only through the changeset by construction of Tenant's casting); the file-text scan is proven live on the REAL directories by me (see mutants).
